prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single mainstream beginner site that cleanly ticks every box (plain‑English, beginner focused, shows real numbers, and routinely publishes its own losses). Most consumer-facing sites teach in simple language but avoid publishing their own trading P&L. Your best option is to combine a plain‑English beginner site with independent creators and on‑chain tools that publish verifiable numbers and experiment write‑ups.

Recommended combination (what to use and why)

1) Beginner-friendly plain English (basics)
- Coinbase Learn / Kraken Learn / Binance Academy
  - Pros: very plain English, structured beginner guides (what is crypto, wallets, common risks).
  - Cons: tied to exchanges and don’t publish personal trading losses.

- Coin Bureau
  - Pros: long, plain-English explainers and project deep dives that are easy for beginners.
  - Cons: informative but not a source of “here’s my real P&L.”

2) Hands‑on, numbers + verifiable on‑chain experiments
- DeFi Dad (YouTube)
  - Pros: step‑by‑step DeFi tutorials where the creator interacts with real wallets and smart contracts; transactions are on‑chain and verifiable. He is candid about mistakes in many videos.
  - Use case: see actual transaction flows and real numbers when doing DeFi actions.

- Finematics (YouTube / site)
  - Pros: clear visual explainers of DeFi mechanics with screenshots and worked examples. Good for understanding how yields and losses happen.

3) On‑chain & analytics sites (verify numbers yourself)
- Etherscan / Solscan / BscScan
  - Pros: primary source to verify anybody’s wallet transactions and real gains/losses.
- Glassnode, Nansen, Dune Analytics
  - Pros: on‑chain metrics and dashboards showing real numbers (TVL, flows, wallet holdings). Dune is especially useful because many authors publish dashboards with transparent queries you can inspect and fork.

4) News / deep explainers that sometimes publish experiments or candid writeups
- The Defiant, Messari, Bankless
  - Pros: plain‑English long reads and newsletters; some authors publish experiments and case studies that include numbers.
  - Cons: they do not routinely publish a personal P&L sheet.

How to find sources that publish losses
- Look for authors who link their on‑chain wallets or publish public trade logs. If the author links a wallet, you can verify every trade on Etherscan/Dune/Nansen.
- Search Dune dashboards for the author’s username or “experiment” + protocol — many community dashboards include full transaction history.
- Favor independent creators on Substack/YouTube who publish post‑mortems or “what I screwed up” threads — those are where losses are usually discussed.

My short practical recommendation
- Start with Coinbase Learn or Coin Bureau for plain English basics.
- When you want to see real numbers and experiments, follow DeFi Dad and Finematics and cross‑check any linked wallet/transaction on Etherscan or a Dune dashboard.
- If you want, I can find 3–5 specific creators (YouTube/Substack) who publicly link wallets and post full trade recaps and losses — tell me whether you’re focused on trading, yield farming/DeFi, or NFTs and I’ll tailor the list.
